Why is the Colosseum full of holes? 🕳️ 8 years of Roman building in 33 seconds. ⏱️

Nero's private lake drained. A concrete ring foundation. Over 100,000 m³ of travertine stacked with no mortar, held together by about 300 tons of iron clamps. 80 arches, 50,000 seats, opened in 80 AD.

The twist: an earthquake in 1349 brought down the south side, the fallen stone was carted off to build churches and palaces, and people hacked out the iron clamps to melt them down. Those holes are where the iron used to be.

Next: the Golden Gate Bridge. Follow so you don't miss it. 👇

yt_description:
Nero's lake drained, a concrete ring foundation, more than 100,000 m³ of travertine set without mortar and pinned with ~300 tons of iron clamps, 80 arches and ~50,000 seats, opened by Titus in 80 AD. After the 1349 earthquake its stone was reused across Rome, and the iron clamps were hacked out, leaving the holes you see today.
